close_reason: Fixed in commit (just landed). memory.rs:612 limit cast now uses the saturating form n.min(usize::MAX as u64) as usize, mirroring canonical mail-server/src/memory.rs:356. Closes the 32-bit drift; chat-server is back in line with the canonical extension-server template.
description:
crate-jmap-chat-server/src/memory.rs:612 — `take(limit.map_or(usize::MAX, |n| n as usize))` where `n: u64`. On 32-bit targets, `n as usize` is a value-changing truncation: any limit > u32::MAX silently wraps to a smaller usize. The canonical sibling crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory.rs:356 uses the safe form: `take(limit.map_or(usize::MAX, |n| n.min(usize::MAX as u64) as usize))` — saturates rather than truncates, and is explicitly documented in the surrounding code (see mail-server:350-353 comment on saturating_neg).

Per the workspace AGENTS.md "Canonical Templates" rule (jmap-mail-server is the canonical extension-server template, jmap-chat-server is a sibling that mirrors it), this is chat-server-local drift: chat-server is wrong relative to canonical. The fix is to copy mail-server's saturating form into chat-server.

Idiomatic Rust: any `u64 as usize` cast on caller-controlled input is suspect; the saturating form makes the cast lossless on every platform Rust supports. The non-saturating form here is also flagged by clippy::cast_possible_truncation under -W clippy::pedantic.

Engineering basis is small (the bug only fires on 32-bit with limit > 4GiB, which is unrealistic for chat) but the fix is a 12-character edit that brings chat-server back in line with canonical mail-server and removes the divergence. No reason to keep the unsafe form.
title: chat-server memory.rs query limit cast truncates on 32-bit where canonical mail-server saturates
